title: What It Takes to Get a Job on Wall Street
summary: Investment banking is more competitive than ever. Jo Constantz breaks down what it takes to get your first job on Wall Street. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US 10-Year Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007 as Fed Looms
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose to the highest in almost two decades, the latest milestone in a bruising global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, mounting debt and inflation.

title: Traders Are at Odds With ECB and BOE on How Far Rates Will Rise
summary: Traders are increasingly diverging from central bankers on the outlook for interest-rate hikes in Europe.

title: French Evening Power Price Nears €300 as Nuclear Output Falls
summary: France’s energy system is facing a tight period this evening as low nuclear availability drives up power prices.

title: SocGen Says Higher Yields May Put AI Debt Capex at Risk
summary: Kokou Agbo-Bloua, global head of economics, cross-asset and quant research at Societe Generale Corporate and Investment Banking, discusses the rising 10-year Treasury yield and its impact on debt-fueled artificial intelligence capex. "If it goes to let's say 5.5% to 6% and growth doesn't pick up, because it's there simply reflecting higher nominal GDP, then you can sort of break the whole economics of AI debt capex," Agbo-Bloua tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Essity Said to Prep for Tissue Exit With Sale, Listing on Table
summary: Essity AB is preparing to kick off the sales process for its consumer tissue business as soon as next month, according to people familiar with the matter, after activist investor Cevian Capital took a minority stake in the Swedish company.

title: Flows Will Return to Private Credit, Blackstone’s Gray Tells NZZ
summary: Blackstone Inc. is working through a backlog of investors who’ve asked to pull cash out of the firm’s flagship private credit fund and is confident the asset class will recover, President and Chief Operating Officer Jon Gray told Swiss newspaper NZZ.

title: India Short-End Bonds Fall Most in Four Years on Cash Drain Plan
summary: Indian bonds slumped after the central bank said it would sell sovereign notes to drain cash from lenders, adding to the supply of debt in a year when the market is already under pressure from record government borrowing.

title: Gold Falls Below $4,300 as Higher Oil Stokes Rate-Hike Bets
summary: Gold held a decline as further disruptions to oil flows from the Middle East reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates as soon as this week.

title: BofA Says Risk of Disorderly Bond Move Trims Excess Bullishness
summary: Exuberance around risk assets is fading as investors worry about a chaotic rise in bond yields and the results of US midterm elections, according to a survey by Bank of America Corp.

title: Home Sales in Canada Decline as Trade War With the US Escalates
summary: Momentum in Canada’s housing market stalled in August as trade talks with the US broke down and the countries levied new tariffs on each other’s goods.

title: Marsh Raises Treasury Allocation to Neutral on Elevated Yields
summary: US investment consultancy Marsh is raising its Treasury allocation in some portfolios recommended to clients, a sign that large investors aim to take advantage of elevated yields.

title: Gabon Bonds Surge After Government Audit Finds Lower Debt Stock
summary: Gabon’s bonds surged after the government announced that an audit found the OPEC member’s debt stock stood at $16.7 billion, almost a fifth below an initial estimate.

title: UK Payrolls Drop More Than Expected
summary: Britain’s employers shed workers at the fastest rate in nine months, with the number of employees on company payrolls slipping 26,000 in August, according to the Office for National Statistics. The drop was worse than the 5,000 drop that economists expected, though the provisional estimates are often revised. Bloomberg's Sam Unsted breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russia’s Nornickel Seeks New Partner to Process Copper in China
summary: Russia’s MMC Norilsk Nickel PJSC is talking with a new Chinese partner about a copper processing deal that would enable it to shut down a heavily polluting plant in the Arctic city of Norilsk.

title: Singapore’s Air Quality Reaches Worst Since 2019
summary:
Singapore is shrouded in haze, with smoke from wildfires in neighboring Indonesia raising islandwide pollution to levels that pose a health risk.

Gabrielle Ng has more.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Puig Agrees to Take Control of Isdin in €1.2 Billion Deal
summary: Puig Brands SA agreed to buy the 50% of Isdin SA it didn’t already own for €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion), giving it full control of the skincare brand. Shares fell.

title: BofA Sees Chance of $150 Oil on Critical Infrastructure Risk
summary: Francisco Blanch, commodities and derivatives research head at BofA Securities, says Brent oil prices could climb as high as $150 a barrel if critical infrastructure, like Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, "is hit on a more permanent basis." Blanch speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
